## Where this course came from

This course began as **BIOS259: The Art of Reproducible Science – A Hands-on
Approach**, a mini-course that Aziz Khan proposed and taught at Stanford
Biosciences in Winter and Autumn of 2024. Much of the original material (slides, exercises,
cheat sheets and setup instructions) is open in the
[bios259-w24 repository](https://github.com/asntech/bios259-w24/) under
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

The Stanford course was developed and taught with help from:

- **Co-instructors:** Clemens - Standord University
- **Teaching assistants:** Alvina, Brennan - Standord University

We thank them, and the students in that first and second cohort whose questions and
feedback shaped the material.

This CBIO7501 version, taught at MBZUAI, is a rebuild rather than a copy. It
adds Pixi as the main environment tool, the *E. coli* LTEE project as one
running example, a Snakemake and Nextflow pipeline, and a Quarto site with
tested tutorials.

This version is desgined in a workshop-style and it reuses and adapts open material from many people. This page
lists all of it. Each adapted page also has an **Adapted from** box at the
bottom, and each slide deck ends with a **Sources** slide.

How we reuse (see `LICENSES.md` in the repository):

- Material under CC BY 4.0, CC0, MIT or BSD licenses is adapted with
  attribution, and we say what we changed.
- Material under a non-commercial or share-alike license, or whose license
  we could not confirm, is **linked, not copied**.
- Third-party figures (journal pages, press photos, comics) are linked with a
  short description, not embedded.

A check (`pixi run check-credits`) fails the website build if a page says it
adapts a source that is missing from this page.

### Pixi documentation: container example (code) {#pixi-docs}

The Dockerfile in the project template (`containers/Dockerfile`, used in
[08 Containers](08-containers.qmd)) adapts the example in the Pixi
documentation, *Containerizing*, <https://pixi.prefix.dev/latest/deployment/container/>.
Copyright (c) 2023, prefix.dev GmbH, [BSD 3-Clause License](https://github.com/prefix-dev/pixi/blob/main/LICENSE).
Changes: the environment name is a build argument, `PATH` is set for
Apptainer, and the project is mounted at run time instead of copied in.

## 3. Data

**LTEE sequencing reads (subset).** Tenaillon O, Barrick JE, Ribeck N,
Deatherage DE, Blanchard JL, Dasgupta A, Wu GC, Wielgoss S, Cruveiller S,
Médigue C, Schneider D, Lenski RE, Reiter T, Mizzi J, Psomopoulos F, Peek R,
Williams J (2019). *Data Carpentry Genomics Curriculum Example Data.*
figshare, dataset, version 3. <https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.7726454.v3>.
License: CC0. We use the file `sub.tar.gz` (file 14418248): trimmed and
subsampled reads (175,000 pairs each) of samples SRR2589044, SRR2584863 and
SRR2584866.

**The experiment behind the data.** Tenaillon O, Barrick JE, Ribeck N, et al.
(2016). Tempo and mode of genome evolution in a 50,000-generation experiment.
*Nature* 536:165–170. <https://doi.org/10.1038/nature18959>. The three runs
we use (SRR2589044, strain REL2181A; SRR2584863, REL7179B; SRR2584866,
REL11365) are in NCBI BioProject PRJNA295606, part of the LTEE umbrella
project PRJNA294072 that the figshare record cites (checked in NCBI on
2026-10-24).

**Reference genome.** *Escherichia coli* B str. REL606, complete genome,
GenBank CP000819.1, assembly GCA_000017985.1 (ASM1798v1), NCBI.
<https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/CP000819.1>. Jeong H, Barbe V, Lee CH,
et al. (2009). Genome sequences of *Escherichia coli* B strains REL606 and
BL21(DE3). *J Mol Biol* 394:644–652. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmb.2009.09.052>.

**The Long-Term Evolution Experiment.** Richard Lenski and colleagues,
<https://lenski.mmg.msu.edu/ecoli/>.

## 5. Figures, images and fonts

- **NBIS figures** (CC BY 4.0): the seven listed under [NBIS](#nbis), stored in
  `assets/images/nbis/` with a README of their sources. Each is shown with the
  line "Figure: NBIS, *Tools for Reproducible Research*, CC BY 4.0".
- **Our own** (CC BY 4.0): the diagrams of images and containers and of Nextflow
  channels and processes (`assets/images/diagrams/`), the LTEE rule graph and
  the LTEE report screenshot, and every chart made from the LTEE data.
- **Linked, not embedded**: third-party figures discussed in the slides (press
  photos, journal pages, comics, figures under other licenses) are described
  on the slide and linked in that deck's Sources slide.
- **Fonts**, served from this site: [Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/) 4.1 (The
  Inter Project Authors) and [JetBrains Mono](https://www.jetbrains.com/lp/mono/)
  2.304 (The JetBrains Mono Project Authors), both under the SIL Open Font
  License 1.1 (`assets/fonts/`, with the license texts).

## 6. Readings

Readings are listed in each lesson under *Further reading*. The core list:

- Noble WS (2009). A quick guide to organizing computational biology projects. *PLoS Comput Biol* 5:e1000424. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1000424>
- Wilson G, Bryan J, Cranston K, Kitzes J, Nederbragt L, Teal TK (2017). Good enough practices in scientific computing. *PLoS Comput Biol* 13:e1005510. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005510>
- Wilkinson MD et al. (2016). The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship. *Sci Data* 3:160018. <https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18>
- Carroll SR et al. (2020). The CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance. *Data Sci J* 19:43. <https://doi.org/10.5334/dsj-2020-043>
- Ziemann M, Poulain P, Bora A (2023). The five pillars of computational reproducibility: bioinformatics and beyond. *Brief Bioinform* 24:bbad375. <https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbad375>
- The Turing Way Community. *The Turing Way: a handbook for reproducible, ethical and collaborative research.* Zenodo. <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3233853>
